newsitem.title: DENMARK: FOCUS - Carlsberg profits up, but wary.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Carlsberg profits up, but wary.

text.p: Danish brewing giant Carlsberg on Monday reported annual net profits hitting a new record high but warned that growing competition, burgeoning promotion costs and fluctuating global economies could hit earnings in future.
In its report for 1995-96 Carlsberg logged net profit of 1.063 billion crowns ($183 million), compared to analysts' expectations of 1.020 and last year's 1.003 billion.
But a commentary on the result said that while overall expectations were for continued growth, a harsh business environment meant that the road ahead could be a rocky one.

"Constantly growing competition combined with the group's commitment to retain its position among the foremost players in the international brewing industry may, also in coming years, lead to declining financial results for brief periods," it said.
The warning weighed on the group's share, taking it at one point down to 371 crowns, from Friday's closing 382 crowns, before it closed at 375.

Operating profit was up to 1.252 billion crowns from the previous year's 1.212 and pre-tax profit up to 1.570 billion crowns from 1.420. Turnover was 18 billion crowns, compared to 1994-95's 17 billion.
"Seen in the light of tough global transitions and major transitions...we are not displeased at the financial result," Carlsberg CEO Poul Svanholm said in a statement.

"Rapidly increasing sales and advertising spending in support of our brands in several core markets was amply offset by an increase in turnover, at the same time the effects of improved productivity are beginning to materialise," he added.
Financial income rose over the past 12 months to 318 million crowns from 208 million, mainly from securities dealings.
Earnings per 20-crown share rose to 16.63 from 15.69 but Carlsberg proposed leaving the dividend unchanged at 17 percent.
The brewer owns 50 percent of Britain's Carlsberg-Tetley, but would hold 20 percent of a larger entity if British regulators allow a merger with Bass to proceed.
The merger was initialled in August but British regulators have yet to rule, prompting Carlsberg to write in protest.
At home, Carlsberg is negotiating with Coca-Cola on expansion of their Danish production and distribution alliance to Norway and Sweden.
Coca-Cola last year ended a 43-year-old licensing deal with Pripps Ringnes, a joint venture of Swedish vehicle maker AB Volvo and Norwegian conglomerate Orkla ASA.
Monday's report said that Carlsberg-Coke talks, initiated last June, continue: "Although they have been positive, these talks have not yet been concluded," it said.
Pripps on Monday said that its talks on winding up the Coke partnership had hit snags but were still in progress.

Looking ahead, Carlsberg said it was considering selling some of the prime Copenhagen property made vacant by relocation of production facilities and expected them to command prices above their book value.
